title: Joker: Folie a Deux and the influence of the last temptation of Christ

commenti.body:
I have yet to see the film but I’ve listened to a bit about it and read a good bit about it and I think your observations seem to follow what I’ve heard, that it’s almost a response to the response of the first film. 

I can’t add much more other than I havn’t seen the film but I wanted to add that i appreciate the effort you put in to the post as I think that’s part of what makes this community great. I imagine if there’s a lack of response it’s due to the fact the movie just came out. I thought you were fairly coherent and despite the broken grammar (which you acknowledged) still appreciate the post and effort.
I don't really buy the whole New Testament - Nietzche thing you tried to connect. I think the movie just tried to buy into the "Joker" hype that nobody expected when the first movie came out.
Yeah I agree this OP sounds AI generated, except for the terrible ideas presented.

moar like folie a deuce amirite?

Exactly what I thought after pondering on the less than stellar response from the fans. The parallels between the conflicts of both characters (Arthur Fleck and Jesus from The Last Temptation of Christ) is striking. People will make a hero/cillian based on their own troubled projections. It's not the person they idolize, but what they have come to expect out of them.
